opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Head office, marketing support and running the global franchising machine — includes $111M of depreciation and amortization.

footerNote: Restaurant costs are shown net of $37M of other operating income (mostly gains on restaurant sales). McDonald's reports in rounded millions: 'Other revenues' is shown as $181M (reported $182M) and net other expense as $402M so each line ties exactly to the reported totals.
oneTimers: Pre-tax charges of $52M ($0.06 per share) for restructuring under the 'Accelerating the Organization' program; the year-ago quarter had $43M of similar charges. Excluding them, operating income rose 4%.
otherDetail: Interest expense of $409M on McDonald's debt, partly offset by $6M of nonoperating income.

segments.name: Franchised restaurants
segments.note: Rent and royalties paid by the local owners who run most McDonald's restaurants — the heart of the business model.

segments.name: Company-owned restaurants
segments.note: Food and drink sold at restaurants McDonald's runs itself.

segments.name: Other revenues
segments.note: Initial fees from new restaurants and other smaller income.

takeaways.text: Global comparable sales rose 1.3% (U.S. +0.8%) — higher checks and favorable product mix offset fewer U.S. guest visits.
takeaways.title: Comps stayed positive

takeaways.text: Diluted EPS was $3.32, up 6%. Excluding $52M of restructuring charges tied to the 'Accelerating the Organization' program, it was $3.38.
takeaways.title: EPS rose 6%

takeaways.text: Franchise revenue — rent and royalties from other people's restaurants — was $4.4B, 62% of all revenue, and nearly pure margin. Company-run stores bring in most of the rest at much thinner margins.
takeaways.title: Franchisees carry the model

verdict: McDonald's grew revenue 4% to $7.1B and squeezed operating profit up 3% — franchise fees did the work while U.S. guest counts stayed soft.
